environment: Primary use of Claude Code: general embedded development, including but not limited to the Yocto Project, and tests on real boards.

Host containment: Claude Code runs as an unprivileged user in a disposable virtual machine. The machine has no sudo, no git credentials, and no cloud credentials. The only credential in it is the login of Claude Code itself. The firewall of the host blocks the local network, any tailnet, and the host. The internet is open, because builds fetch source code from many hosts.
Source control: Claude commits to local repositories in the workspace. Claude does not push. The owner fetches the commits from this machine, reviews them, and pushes them.
Network posture: Fetching source code from public hosts is expected, for example GitHub and kernel.org. Sending workspace data to any host outside the board network is not expected.

Trusted internal destinations: the board network 10.250.1.0/24 on a separate Ethernet card. This machine is 10.250.1.1 and runs the DHCP and TFTP servers there. The network is inside the trust boundary for data flow. The owner owns every host in it, and none is a production or shared system. Claude may log in to these hosts, write files to them, reflash them, reboot them, and run tests on them, for example with ssh, scp, and serial or network consoles.
Trusted source hosts: git.yoctoproject.org, git.openembedded.org, github.com/openembedded, github.com/yoctoproject, and git.kernel.org. Claude may add a layer from these hosts.

Hardware: The machine may have USB serial adapters (/dev/ttyUSB*), SD card multiplexers, and development boards that the owner connects. Writing an image to an SD card on a multiplexer and power-cycling a board are normal tasks.
allow: Running bitbake, devtool, kas, whisk, bitbake-setup, repo sync, git clone, oe-init-build-env, runqemu, wic, and devtool deploy-target is expected. So is running make or configure in a cloned kernel or U-Boot tree. This includes the build steps that run the fetched code. It covers sources that the project files already name (kas files, bblayers.conf, repo manifests, and recipes), sources that the owner named, and layers from the trusted source hosts. If Claude adds or changes a layer, SRC_URI, SRCREV, or manifest entry to point at any other host in this session, the build is not covered. Also not covered: running a downloaded script or binary outside a build, and repo sync --force-sync, repo sync -d, and kas --update, which can discard uncommitted work.

Rewriting local commits with git rebase, git commit --amend, and git reset is expected only when this session created every rewritten commit. git reset --hard is expected only when the working tree has no uncommitted changes.

Serving build artifacts from 10.250.1.1 to the board network (TFTP, NFS, and HTTP) is expected, including files in the TFTP root. Changing the configuration of the DHCP, TFTP, or NFS server is not expected.
